title: Great Mosque of Kairouan
summary: The Great Mosque of Kairouan in Tunisia was founded by Uqba ibn Nafi in 670 AD and given its final plan under the governor Ziadat Allah Ibn al-Aghlab in 836–841. Its square minaret, 31.5 m high, stands in the middle of the north portico of the courtyard and is attributed by most archaeologists to Ziyadat Allah I.

uncertainty.note: Founding in 50 AH / 670 AD per the Tunisian heritage page; the final plan dates to 836–841 and the minaret to 836 (Qantara). End is the present.

where.modern_name: Great Mosque of Kairouan, Kairouan, Tunisia
where.historical_name: Great Mosque of Kairouan, Ifriqiya, rebuilt under Ziadat Allah Ibn al-Aghlab (836–841)

importance.justification: A mosque founded in 670 whose present plan dates to 836–841, with a 31.5 m minaret.

sources.title: Qantara - Minaret of the Great Mosque of Kairouan
sources.author: Qantara (Mediterranean Heritage, qantara-med.org)

reviewer_note: Shape choice: tower (square-plan minaret in three storeys); the model describes the minaret only, not the 126 x 75 m mosque. Least sure: the Qantara page names no publisher, and UNESCO and Archnet pages could not be opened. Minaret attribution is debated (Al-Bakri credits Hisham, most archaeologists Ziyadat Allah I); the third storey was probably remodelled in the Hafsid period.
